rationale:
Split into two children. The supplied proof has three separable layers. (i) Step 4 is pure linear algebra of unit orientations: ξ ≠ 0 and ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1. (ii) Steps 3–7 prove the analytic local statement: if T vanishes on a relatively compact open W, then H^n(M ∩ W) = 0. (iii) Steps 1–2 are the countable reduction from spt T to the members of 𝒲.

Layer (i) is exactly the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.imsupp_unit_orientation_ne_zero_norm_le_one (DAG node root.half_space_cone_lies_in_boundary-a1.imrep_support_eq_measure_support-a1.unit_orientation_nonzero_bounded-a1, status accepted, candidate 2e5d20d). It is proposed under the same name with the byte-identical frozen type, which was checked against dag.json. The controller's _existing_lean_name_problem/_accepted_checkpoint therefore reuse it instead of re-proving it. Its commit is not an ancestor of this node's proof base c36d11c. Without the split, the parent would have to re-prove that lemma inline.

Layer (ii) is a genuine, reusable local support lemma and becomes the new child imrep_carrier_inter_null_of_vanishesOn. The name is globally unique: it appears in none of the 198 DAG nodes and none of the 238 git refs. The similar node imsupp_measure_eq_zero_of_vanishesOn is still decomposing, is unaccepted and has a different type, so it cannot be shared.

Layer (iii) stays in the parent, exactly as in supplied steps 1–2:
- M ∖ spt T ⊆ M ∩ zeroRegion T, because M ⊆ U.
- zeroRegion T = ⋃₀𝒲 = ⋃₀𝒯 for a countable 𝒯 ⊆ 𝒲 (TopologicalSpace.isOpen_sUnion_countable).
- Each W ∈ 𝒯 is open with closure W compact and contained in U, and T vanishes on W. So the new child gives H^n(M ∩ W) = 0.
- measure_biUnion_null_iff then gives H^n(M ∖ spt T) = 0.
Hence the two children imply the selected statement by the supplied proof itself, not by an ancestor's argument.

subproblems.title: A unit orientation of a plane is a nonzero n-vector of norm at most one
subproblems.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers. Let ξ ∈ Λ_n(ℝ^P) = MultiVector P n, i.e. a continuous linear functional on the normed space Λ^n(ℝ^P) = Covector (Euclid P) n of continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P (both with Mathlib's operator norms), and let Q be a linear subspace of ℝ^P. Suppose ξ is a unit orientation of Q (IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q). That is, there is an orthonormal family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) in ℝ^P spanning Q such that either ξ(α) = α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for every n-covector α, or ξ(α) = −α(τ_1, …, τ_n) for every α. Then ξ ≠ 0 and ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (ξ : MultiVector P n) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)), IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q → ξ ≠ 0 ∧ ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: step 4 of the parent proof (Simon Ch. 6, 1.1 and 1.7: a unit orientation is ξ = ±τ_1∧⋯∧τ_n for an orthonormal basis τ of the plane). This is the comparator-accepted declaration Submission.imsupp_unit_orientation_ne_zero_norm_le_one, with identical frozen type, reused here.
Notation. Λ^n := Covector (Euclid P) n is the space of continuous alternating n-linear forms on ℝ^P, with the operator norm ‖α‖ = inf{C ≥ 0 : |α(w)| ≤ C·∏_i ‖w_i‖ for all w}. Λ_n := MultiVector P n = (Λ^n →L[ℝ] ℝ), with its operator norm. For α ∈ Λ^n write α(τ) := α(τ_1, …, τ_n). The hypothesis that τ spans Q is not used.
1. Unpacking. By IsUnitOrientationOf ξ Q there is a family τ = (τ_1, …, τ_n) in ℝ^P with these properties:
- τ is orthonormal: ‖τ_a‖ = 1 for every a, and ⟨τ_a, τ_b⟩ = 0 for a ≠ b.
- Either ξ(α) = α(τ) for every α ∈ Λ^n, or ξ(α) = −α(τ) for every α ∈ Λ^n.
In both cases |ξ(α)| = |α(τ)| for every α; in the second case this uses |−t| = |t|.
2. Norm bound. Let α ∈ Λ^n. By the operator-norm inequality for continuous alternating maps (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm) and ‖τ_a‖ = 1:
|ξ(α)| = |α(τ)| ≤ ‖α‖·∏_a ‖τ_a‖ = ‖α‖ = 1·‖α‖.
Since this holds for every α, ContinuousLinearMap.opNorm_le_bound with the constant 1 ≥ 0 gives ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1.
3. The determinant covector. Let m(w_1, …, w_n) := ∏_{a=1}^n ⟨τ_a, w_a⟩. This is a continuous n-linear form: the product form ContinuousMultilinearMap.mkPiAlgebra ℝ (Fin n) ℝ composed in slot a with the continuous linear functional innerSL ℝ τ_a = ⟨τ_a, ·⟩ (compContinuousLinearMap). Let β_τ := Alt(m) be its alternatization (ContinuousMultilinearMap.alternatization). Then β_τ is a continuous alternating n-linear form, so β_τ ∈ Λ^n. By alternatization_apply_apply,
β_τ(w) = Σ_{σ ∈ S_n} sign(σ)·∏_a ⟨τ_a, w_{σ(a)}⟩ = det(⟨τ_a, w_b⟩)_{a,b}.
For n = 0 this is the constant 1.
4. β_τ(τ) = 1. Expand β_τ(τ) = Σ_σ sign(σ)·∏_a ⟨τ_a, τ_{σ(a)}⟩.
- If σ ≠ id, choose a with σ(a) ≠ a. Orthonormality gives ⟨τ_a, τ_{σ(a)}⟩ = 0, so that product is 0 (Finset.prod_eq_zero).
- The term σ = id is sign(id)·∏_a ⟨τ_a, τ_a⟩ = ∏_a ‖τ_a‖² = 1.
Hence β_τ(τ) = 1 (Finset.sum_eq_single). This includes n = 0, where S_0 = {id} and the empty product is 1.
5. Nonvanishing. By step 1, |ξ(β_τ)| = |β_τ(τ)| = 1. If ξ were 0, then ξ(β_τ) = 0, which gives 0 = 1, a contradiction. Hence ξ ≠ 0.
6. Steps 5 and 2 together give ξ ≠ 0 ∧ ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1.
proof_key_steps: Unpack IsUnitOrientationOf: ξ(α) = ±α(τ) for every covector α, with τ orthonormal, so |ξ(α)| = |α(τ)|.
β_τ := alternatization of w ↦ ∏_a⟨τ_a, w_a⟩ (mkPiAlgebra ∘ innerSL) is an n-covector with β_τ(w) = det(⟨τ_a, w_b⟩).
Orthonormality kills every σ ≠ id, so β_τ(τ) = 1.

subproblems.title: The carrier is H^n-null inside a relatively compact open set on which the current vanishes
subproblems.statement: Let P, n be natural numbers, U ⊆ ℝ^P any set and W ⊆ ℝ^P. Let T ∈ 𝒟_n(U) be a GeometricCurrentOn U n, and let R = (M, θ, ξ) be an integer multiplicity triple in U (IMRep U n) representing T: T(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^n(x) for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) = TestFormOn U n. Assume W is open, closure W is compact, closure W ⊆ U, and T vanishes on W, i.e. T(ω) = 0 for every ω ∈ 𝒟^n(U) with tsupport ω ⊆ W. Then H^n(M ∩ W) = 0, where H^n = μHE[n] is Mathlib's normalized n-dimensional Hausdorff measure.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P n : ℕ) (U W : Set (Euclid P)) (T : GeometricCurrentOn U n) (R : IMRep U n), R.Represents T → IsOpen W → IsCompact (closure W) → closure W ⊆ U → T.VanishesOn W → μHE[n] (R.carrier ∩ W) = 0
subproblems.natural_proof:
Source: steps 3–7 of the parent proof, for one fixed member W of the family 𝒲 (Simon 6.2.11 with 6.3.1 and 6.3.2(3); book/chapter-06.txt lines 296–303 and 763–768). Simon uses without proof that an integer multiplicity current carries no mass where it vanishes.
This proof uses the sibling unit_orientation_bounds: every ξ_0 ∈ Λ_n with IsUnitOrientationOf ξ_0 Q satisfies ξ_0 ≠ 0 and ‖ξ_0‖ ≤ 1.
Notation.
- M := R.carrier, θ := R.mult : ℝ^P → ℕ, ξ := R.orient : ℝ^P → Λ_n.
- Λ^n := Covector (Euclid P) n and Λ_n := MultiVector P n = Λ^n →L[ℝ] ℝ, both with operator norms.
- H^n := μHE[n], C := closure W and ν := H^n⌞(M ∩ C) = μHE[n].restrict (M ∩ C).
Fields of R used:
- M is measurable (measurableSet_carrier) and θ is measurable (measurable_mult).
- θ(x) > 0 for x ∈ M (mult_pos).
- ∫⁻_{M∩K} θ dH^n ≠ ∞ for every compact K ⊆ U (locallyIntegrable_mult).
- ξ is H^n⌞M-a.e. strongly measurable (aestronglyMeasurable_orient).
- For H^n⌞M-a.e. x there is a subspace Q with IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ x) Q (orients).
Representation: T(ω) = R.action(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(ω(x)) dH^n(x) for every ω ∈ TestFormOn U n. Openness of U is not needed.
1. Measurability. M ∩ C is measurable because M is measurable and C is closed. W is measurable because it is open.
2. ν is finite and θ ∈ L¹(ν). C is compact and C ⊆ U, so locallyIntegrable_mult with K = C gives ∫⁻ θ dν = ∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dH^n ≠ ∞. For x ∈ M ∩ C, θ(x) is a positive integer, so 1 ≤ θ(x). Hence
ν(ℝ^P) = H^n(M ∩ C) = ∫⁻_{M∩C} 1 dH^n ≤ ∫⁻_{M∩C} θ dH^n < ∞ (setLIntegral_mono),
so ν is a finite measure. The real function x ↦ θ(x) is measurable and ∫⁻ θ dν < ∞, so it is ν-integrable (integrable_toReal_of_lintegral_ne_top, using (θ(x) : [0,∞]).toReal = θ(x)).
3. Facts holding ν-a.e. Since M ∩ C ⊆ M, ν ≤ H^n⌞M (Measure.restrict_mono), so every H^n⌞M-a.e. property holds ν-a.e. (ae_mono).
- By orients and the sibling lemma, ξ(x) ≠ 0 and ‖ξ(x)‖ ≤ 1 for H^n⌞M-a.e. x, hence for ν-a.e. x.
- ξ is ν-a.e. strongly measurable (AEStronglyMeasurable.mono_measure).
- ν-a.e. x lies in M ∩ C (ae_restrict_mem, using step 1).
4. Scalar components are integrable. Fix α ∈ Λ^n and put f_α(x) := θ(x)·ξ(x)(α) ∈ ℝ.
- f_α is ν-a.e. strongly measurable: it is the product of the measurable θ with x ↦ ξ(x)(α), which is ξ composed with the continuous linear evaluation L ↦ L(α).
- For ν-a.e. x, ContinuousLinearMap.le_opNorm and step 3 give |f_α(x)| = θ(x)·|ξ(x)(α)| ≤ θ(x)·‖ξ(x)‖·‖α‖ ≤ ‖α‖·θ(x).
- Since ‖α‖·θ ∈ L¹(ν) by step 2, f_α ∈ L¹(ν) (Integrable.mono').
In particular f_α is locally integrable on W with respect to ν (Integrable.locallyIntegrable, then LocallyIntegrable.locallyIntegrableOn).
5. Testing T. Let α ∈ Λ^n, and let g : ℝ^P → ℝ be C^∞ with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ W. Define ω(x) := g(x)·α.
- ω is C^∞ (g times a constant) and has compact support (HasCompactSupport.smul_right).
- tsupport ω ⊆ tsupport g ⊆ W ⊆ C ⊆ U (tsupport_smul_subset_left).
So ω ∈ TestFormOn U n with tsupport ω ⊆ W, and T(ω) = 0 because T vanishes on W. By the representation,
0 = T(ω) = ∫_M θ(x)·ξ(x)(g(x)·α) dH^n(x).
If x ∈ M \ (M ∩ C), then x ∉ C ⊇ W, so x ∉ tsupport g and g(x) = 0 (image_eq_zero_of_notMem_tsupport). The integrand there is θ(x)·ξ(x)(0) = 0. Since M is measurable and M ∩ C ⊆ M, the integral over M equals the integral over M ∩ C (setIntegral_eq_of_subset_of_forall_sdiff_eq_zero, valid with or without integrability). By linearity of ξ(x), θ(x)·ξ(x)(g(x)·α) = g(x)·f_α(x). Hence
∫ g(x)·f_α(x) dν(x) = ∫_{M∩C} θ(x)·ξ(x)(g(x)·α) dH^n(x) = 0.
6. Fundamental lemma. ℝ^P is a finite-dimensional real normed space with its Borel σ-algebra, and W is open. By step 4, f_α is locally integrable on W for ν. By step 5, ∫ g·f_α dν = 0 for every C^∞ g with compact support and tsupport g ⊆ W. Mathlib's IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero (real-valued case) then gives: for ν-a.e. x, x ∈ W ⇒ θ(x)·ξ(x)(α) = 0. For ν-a.e. x also x ∈ M (step 3), so θ(x) ≥ 1 > 0. Therefore, for ν-a.e. x, x ∈ W ⇒ ξ(x)(α) = 0.
7. Λ^n is finite-dimensional. Let e_1, …, e_P be the standard basis of ℝ^P. Define the linear map Φ : Λ^n → ℝ^{(Fin n → Fin P)} by Φ(α)(I) := α(e_{I(1)}, …, e_{I(n)}). Suppose Φ(α) = Φ(β). Then the underlying alternating maps of α and β agree on every tuple of basis vectors, so they are equal (Module.Basis.ext_alternating), and hence α = β (ContinuousAlternatingMap.toAlternatingMap_injective). Thus Φ is an injective linear map into a finite-dimensional space, so Λ^n is finite-dimensional (FiniteDimensional.of_injective). Fix a basis α_1, …, α_N of Λ^n (Module.finBasis).
8. Conclusion. Apply step 6 to each α_k and intersect the finitely many full-measure sets (ae_all_iff): for ν-a.e. x, x ∈ W ⇒ ξ(x)(α_k) = 0 for all k. Take x in this set that also satisfies ξ(x) ≠ 0 (step 3); ν-a.e. x qualifies. If x ∈ W, the linear functional ξ(x) on Λ^n vanishes on a basis, so ξ(x) = 0 (Basis.ext for the underlying linear map, then ContinuousLinearMap.coe_injective). This contradicts ξ(x) ≠ 0. Hence ν-a.e. x satisfies x ∉ W, i.e. ν(W) = 0 (measure_eq_zero_iff_ae_notMem). As W is measurable, ν(W) = H^n(W ∩ (M ∩ C)) (Measure.restrict_apply). Since W ⊆ closure W = C, W ∩ (M ∩ C) = M ∩ W. Therefore H^n(M ∩ W) = 0.
proof_key_steps: ν := H^n⌞(M ∩ closure W) is a finite measure and θ ∈ L¹(ν), because closure W is a compact subset of U (locallyIntegrable_mult) and θ ≥ 1 on M.
By R.orients and unit_orientation_bounds, ξ ≠ 0 and ‖ξ‖ ≤ 1 hold ν-a.e., so f_α = θ·ξ(α) is ν-integrable and |f_α| ≤ ‖α‖θ, for every covector α.
For g ∈ C_c^∞ with tsupport g ⊆ W, the form ω = g·α lies in TestFormOn U n with support in W, so 0 = T(ω) = ∫_M θ ξ(gα) dH^n = ∫ g f_α dν.
The fundamental lemma on the open set W (IsOpen.ae_eq_zero_of_integral_contDiff_smul_eq_zero) gives ξ(α) = 0 ν-a.e. on W, since θ > 0 on M.
Λ^n is finite-dimensional (Basis.ext_alternating); testing a basis gives ξ = 0 ν-a.e. on W, contradicting ξ ≠ 0, so H^n(M ∩ W) = ν(W) = 0.
